currentContext.business: Established in 1988, the Company operates across multiple wellness and nutrition segments, including sugar substitutes, low sugar, energy drinks, nutritional drinks, low-calorie foods, protein snacks and bars and personal care products. It is focused on developing, manufacturing, marketing and distributing differentiated health and wellness products, driven by innovation, quality and consumer-centricity, serving consumers across urban, semi-urban and rural India and in over 44 countries internationally. During the year the Company acquired Comfort Click Limited, United Kingdom and its three subsidiaries, adding a digital-first Vitamins, Minerals and Supplements portfolio spanning adult nutrition, kids wellness and pet health across the UK, EU and USA.

Remuneration policy intent is set out separately: the Nomination and Remuneration Committee follows a structured, performance-driven Nomination and Remuneration Policy that aligns pay with performance and long-term business objectives, balances fixed and variable pay components and ensures transparency, fairness and compliance. Related-party dealings are conducted in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis, with no contracts or arrangements entered into on a non-arm's length basis during the year. Beyond this, the routed governance sections do not set out an explicit payout-ratio, buyback, debt or reinvestment philosophy.|2030 climate targets against an FY2022 baseline: 50% reduction in GHG emissions from direct operations, 50% improvement in energy efficiency and 50% renewable energy share.|Governance levers on climate: SBTi commitment, internal carbon pricing and climate scenario analysis aligned to TCFD for resilience planning.|Water stewardship target: commitment to a 25% reduction in water intensity by 2030 versus the FY2022 baseline, with enterprise-wide water risk management and expansion of recycling/reuse and Zero Liquid Discharge / advanced treatment systems across sites where feasible (ZLD progress already underway).|Circular packaging roadmap prioritising recyclable/optimised packaging and sustainability-led innovation, continued Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) compliance through authorised partners, and packaging-reduction projects across key brands to cut material use at source.|Effluent, wastewater quality and chemical stewardship (including hazardous waste) identified as a material responsible business conduct issue, given stricter discharge norms and community sensitivity.|External assurance: SGS India Pvt. Ltd provides reasonable assurance on BRSR Core parameters, with the BRSR reported on a consolidated basis covering the parent, its wholly owned subsidiaries, their manufacturing facilities and national and international offices (excluding four wholly owned subsidiaries without physical operations).|Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, with published Human Rights, Public Policy, CSR, POSH, Whistle Blower and vendor code of conduct policies.
currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 was an acquisition-led expansion year rather than a bricks-and-mortar capex year: the routed sections describe no new plant, line or capacity project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. The defining move was the acquisition of Comfort Click, which expanded the Company's footprint across the United Kingdom, Europe and the United States of America and significantly enhanced its participation in the high-growth Vitamins, Minerals & Supplements category spanning adult nutrition, kids wellness and pet health, while accelerating overseas digital capability through Comfort Click's Direct-to-Consumer and e-commerce-led operating model. Comfort Click brings three brands - WeightWorld, Maxmedix and Animigo - and was recognised among the Financial Times' Top 1000 fastest growing companies in Europe for three consecutive years. Post acquisition, the WeightWorld brand expanded its European footprint by entering Poland, Finland and Portugal, and WeightWorld and Maxmedix were launched on Boots UK and established a presence on Amazon UAE. Internationally the Company continued to strengthen its footprint across the SAARC, Middle East & Africa, Southeast Asia and Indian Subcontinent Cluster regions through expansion into new geographies and region-specific innovation, and launched RiteBite Max Protein across nine international markets within the first year of that acquisition. Integration rather than construction drove domestic footprint work: the Company implemented rapid integration through the voluntary liquidation of Naturell (India) Private Limited, aligning operations with Zydus Wellness' enterprise-wide systems, distribution network and operating processes to unlock synergies across manufacturing, supply chain and go-to-market infrastructure. Capability build-out continued through the state-of-the-art R&D facility at Ahmedabad, which underpins a strong new product pipeline that could be launched at an appropriate time based on market requirements, and through a channel restructuring in which the Company transitioned from a distribution-led model to direct relationships with all modern trade and e-commerce partners, improving supply chain efficiency, product availability and lead times. Historical facility milestones referenced in the Corporate Overview are the new production facility in Sikkim - Unit-I and, later, the set-up of a new production facility in Sikkim - Unit-II alongside the launch of Sugar Free Green with Stevia; the physical distribution backbone comprises 25 integrated warehouses supporting both ambient and cold-chain categories.

risks.risk: Dependence on a few key brands
risks.note: A significant portion of the Company's revenue is derived from a few key brands; any disruption in supply, quality, competitive positioning or loss of consumer confidence in these brands could adversely impact business performance, growth momentum and market share. Mitigated through brand rejuvenation, continuous innovation, sustained marketing investment and portfolio diversification into adjacent offerings under established brand platforms.

risks.risk: Seasonal demand variability and climate-related risk
risks.note: Performance of brands such as Glucon-D and Nycil is significantly influenced by the timely onset and intensity of the Indian summer; any delay, shortening or shift in seasonal conditions may impact demand, sales volumes and inventory management. Mitigated through a flexible supply chain, improved forecasting, inventory optimisation and by deliberately reducing the saliency of seasonal products and acquiring non-seasonal portfolios.

risks.risk: Product quality, regulatory compliance and product-claim litigation
risks.note: Failure to meet standards established by regulatory authorities may result in regulatory actions, product recalls, penalties or litigation from customers, and the Company faces potential litigation risk relating to product claims made to consumers. Managed via a quality and compliance framework, global food safety standards, self-inspection, a dedicated regulatory affairs team and product-recall insurance.

risks.risk: Intellectual property misuse and counterfeit products
risks.note: Strong brand equity exposes the Company to unauthorised or illegitimate use of its brand name, packaging designs and other IP by third parties; counterfeit manufacture and distribution threaten brand credibility and can cause loss of sales, dilution of brand equity and erosion of consumer trust. Addressed through systematic IP registrations, market monitoring, timely legal action and distribution-network awareness.

Exposure to international trade disputes, protectionist policies, sudden tariff/duty changes and non-tariff barriers, plus political instability, military conflicts, currency volatility and inflation, can raise input and freight costs, disrupt supply chains and restrict market access. Mitigated through diversification of sourcing and manufacturing locations, localisation of manufacturing to reduce FX exposure, portfolio diversification and calibrated geographic expansion into relatively stable, high-potential markets.

The supply network is exposed to physical disruptions, environmental or industrial accidents, labour unrest, trade restrictions and operational challenges at key suppliers, which may impact manufacturing efficiency, logistics and timely delivery. Mitigated through an adaptive and distributed manufacturing footprint, diversified sourcing, inventory buffers and multiple sourcing options for critical inputs.

risks.risk: Under-penetration of categories and market development burden
risks.note: Certain categories the Company operates in remain under-penetrated, which may challenge growth aspirations in the near term through slower adoption rates, extended consumer education cycles and higher investment required for category expansion - while also representing the long-term growth opportunity.

risks.risk: Consumer trust, brand reputation and media-related risk
risks.note: Consumer healthcare and wellness products depend heavily on consumer trust; adverse publicity from misinformation, regulatory scrutiny, influencer backlash or social media controversy can rapidly impact brand perception, consumer confidence and sales. Managed through a crisis communication and response framework and active monitoring of digital platforms and online sentiment.

Increasing digitalisation of business processes and hybrid working raise exposure to cyber-attacks, unauthorised access and misuse of sensitive information, which could disrupt operations, compromise data integrity and confidentiality and damage stakeholder trust. Managed through information security frameworks, advanced security tools and controls, continuous monitoring, periodic system upgrades and employee awareness.

one-line thesis: Zydus Wellness delivered robust top-line growth (62% YoY) driven by the Comfort Click acquisition and strong performance in skin/protein segments, though reported PAT declined 5.8% due to one-off amortization and labor code impacts. The core narrative remains the successful de-risking of weather-dependent seasonal brands through high-margin digital-first international and domestic adjacencies, with operating leverage expected to re-accelerate once seasonal headwinds normalize.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +62.1% YoY (Q4), +46.4% YoY (FY26); EBITDA: INR 2,701 mn (+42.2% YoY Q4), Margin ~13-14% (impacted by mix); PAT (Reported): -5.8% YoY (Q4), -43.2% YoY (FY26) due to amortization of acquired brands, new labor code one-offs, and liquidation costs; PAT (Normalized): +17% YoY (Q4), +2.3% YoY (FY26); Order Book: N/A (FMCG); Net Debt: Elevated temporarily due to GBP bridge loan for Comfort Click acquisition, now refinanced to lower-cost Euro facility.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Double-digit expected for non-seasonal portfolio; Seasonal recovery hoped from May onwards; Margin: Aspirational 17-18% long-term, near-term pressured by seasonal mix but gross margins healthy; Order Inflow: Strong momentum in Quick Commerce (7-8% of total sales); Capex/Commissioning: Focus on AI-led media allocation and new product launches rather than heavy manufacturing capex.
order book & pipeline: N/A - FMCG business model driven by distribution reach and inventory turnover rather than order book. Quick commerce contribution at 7-8% of total domestic sales, representing 44-45% of e-commerce channel.
segment / subsidiary detail: Domestic: +1.7% YoY (Seasonal -9.8%, Skin/Hair +39.7%, Food/Nutrition +9.4%). International (incl. Comfort Click): +31.4% YoY like-for-like. Comfort Click: EPS accretive in Q4, expanding into new European markets plus US/UAE bets. RiteBite: Outperforming with >2x pre-acquisition CAGR, expanding into RTD beverages and chips. Everyuth: Double-digit growth driven by tan removal segment. Sugar Free: Market share +24 bps, D'lite range showing high double-digit growth.
growth verticals / optionality: Geographic expansion of Comfort Click into US/UAE; Category expansion for RiteBite (RTD, chips) and Glucon-D (performance hydration 'Recharge'); New brand 'Cuticolor' in derma-supported hair color; Deepening quick commerce penetration which favors their premium/on-the-go portfolio.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margins remained healthy despite seasonal mix drag. EBITDA margin pressure stems from high fixed cost absorption in underperforming seasonal units and increased amortization of intangible assets from acquisitions. One-time costs include new labor code implementation and Naturell India liquidation. Management expects operating leverage to play out as scale increases and seasonal volatility normalizes.
capex / expansion: Capital allocation focused on M&A (Comfort Click) and brand building. No significant greenfield manufacturing capex highlighted; growth driven by innovation, digital marketing spend, and distribution expansion in organized trade/e-commerce.
capital allocation: Strategic acquisition of Comfort Click funded via low-cost bridge loan (GBP) refinanced to Euro facility. Continued investment in R&D for new product launches (RTD, skincare variants). Divestment/liquidation of non-core subsidiary (Naturell India).
risks & watch-items: Weather dependency for ~30% of portfolio (Glucon-D/Nycil) causing quarterly volatility; Integration risks with international D2C operations; Currency fluctuation (GBP/EUR vs INR) impacting translated earnings; Intense competition in protein snacking and skincare segments; Regulatory changes in labor codes affecting cost structure.
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term structural growth drivers and portfolio diversification benefits; Pragmatic about short-term weather-related misses; Emphasizing data-driven decision making and AI-led marketing efficiency; Committed to profitable growth over blunt volume expansion.
non-obvious takeaways: The 'seasonal' drag is masking a fundamentally stronger underlying business where normalized PAT grew 17% in Q4. The Comfort Click acquisition is already EPS accretive within 7 months, faster than typical integration timelines. Quick commerce is not just a channel but a strategic moat, contributing nearly half of all e-commerce sales and favoring Zydus's premium, small-pack, and impulse-buy SKUs over traditional general trade competitors.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Zydus Wellness Limited is an Ahmedabad-headquartered consumer health and wellness FMCG company that develops, manufactures, markets and distributes differentiated wellness products across sugar substitutes, nutrition, personal care and, following the Comfort Click acquisition, vitamins, minerals …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 1988, the Company operates across multiple wellness and nutrition segments, including sugar substitutes, low sugar, energy drinks, nutritional drinks, low-calorie foods, protein snacks and bars and personal care products. It is focused on developing, manufacturing, marketing and distributing differentiated health and wellness products, driven by innovation, quality and consumer-centricity, serving consumers across urban, semi-urban and rural India and in over 44 countries internationally. During the year the Company acquired Comfort Click Limited, United Kingdom and its three subsidiaries, adding a digital-first Vitamins, Minerals and Supplements portfolio spanning adult nutrition, kids wellness and pet health across the UK, EU and USA.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Domestic: +1.7% YoY (Seasonal -9.8%, Skin/Hair +39.7%, Food/Nutrition +9.4%). International (incl. Comfort Click): +31.4% YoY like-for-like. order_book.body: N/A - FMCG business model driven by distribution reach and inventory turnover rather than order book. Quick commerce contribution at 7-8% of total domestic sales, representing 44-45% of e-commerce channel.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Double-digit expected for non-seasonal portfolio; Seasonal recovery hoped from May onwards; Margin: Aspirational 17-18% long-term, near-term pressured by seasonal mix but gross margins healthy; Order Inflow: Strong momentum in Quick Commerce (7-8% of total sales); Capex/Commissioning: Focus on AI-led media allocation and new product launches rather than heavy manufacturing capex.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Geographic expansion of Comfort Click into US/UAE; Category expansion for RiteBite (RTD, chips) and Glucon-D (performance hydration 'Recharge'); New brand 'Cuticolor' in derma-supported hair color; Deepening quick commerce penetration which favors their premium/on-the-go portfolio.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic mix is shifting to organised channels - 'the domestic business continued to witness a steady shift towards organised channels, with saliency improving to 30% in FY26 from 24% in FY25, driven by premiumisation as well as strong growth in modern trade and e-commerce channels'
- Seasonal brands were hit by weather - domestic seasonal brands declined, 'primarily impacted by early and prolonged rainfall', while skin and hair care and food and nutrition brands grew
- International business, including Comfort Click, delivered like-to-like growth well ahead of the domestic business, making global expansion the principal growth driver
- Margin lever from input costs - 'the Company benefited from a gradual decline in prices of key inputs such as dextrose monohydrate and stevia', alongside strategic hedging initiatives, optimisation of product mix toward higher-margin offerings and calibrated pricing strategies, producing consistent margin expansion across all four quarters
- Watch-item on inputs - 'price volatility particularly in edible oils and milk continued to pose challenges', mitigated by long-term procurement contracts, inventory buffers and supplier-base diversification
- Profitability was weighed down by higher finance costs from the acquisition, initially funded through a GBP bridge loan and subsequently refinanced into a lower-cost EUR loan towards the end of Q4 FY26
- The Comfort Click acquisition was cash EPS accretive in FY 2025-26 and is expected to become EPS accretive from the next financial year
- Innovation engine as a demand driver - a broad spectrum of new product introductions and portfolio enhancements, with positive consumer response to most launches
- Indian macro tailwind - India is projected to grow at 6.52-6.91% in FY 2026-27 as the fastest-growing major economy; GST rate reduction and income tax slab revisions are expected to boost demand, enhance disposable incomes and support discretionary spending and domestic consumption
- Rural employment gains and rising female labour force participation are described as an important supportive factor for consumption-led sectors such as FMCG
- FMCG channel shift - quick commerce, e-commerce and modern trade sustained strong growth momentum; e-commerce penetration increased significantly across metro markets and modern trade rebounded in the second half
- Consumer preference is moving toward convenience, health and wellness-oriented products, with premium breakfast cereals, immunity products and low-sugar offerings recording healthy growth
- Near-term sector risks flagged: commodity price volatility, weather disruptions and global macroeconomic uncertainties, with pricing power constrained in value-oriented categories amid heightened price sensitivity and competitive intensity
- GST 2.0 implementation caused temporary trade-channel disruption and short-term inventory corrections, particularly in traditional trade, which stabilised over subsequent quarters

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margins remained healthy despite seasonal mix drag. EBITDA margin pressure stems from high fixed cost absorption in underperforming seasonal units and increased amortization of intangible assets from acquisitions. One-time costs include new labor code implementation and Naturell India liquidation. Management expects operating leverage to play out as scale increases and seasonal volatility normalizes.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Strategic acquisition of Comfort Click funded via low-cost bridge loan (GBP) refinanced to Euro facility. Continued investment in R&D for new product launches (RTD, skincare variants). Divestment/liquidation of non-core subsidiary (Naturell India).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 was an acquisition-led expansion year rather than a bricks-and-mortar capex year: the routed sections describe no new plant, line or capacity project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. The defining move was the acquisition of Comfort Click, which expanded the Company's footprint across the United Kingdom, Europe and the United States of America and significantly enhanced its participation in the high-growth Vitamins, Minerals & Supplements category spanning adult nutrition, kids wellness and pet health, while accelerating overseas digital capability through Comfort Click's Direct-to-Consumer and e-commerce-led operating model. Comfort Click brings three brands - WeightWorld, Maxmedix and Animigo - and was recognised among the Financial Times' Top 1000 fastest growing companies in Europe for three consecutive years. Post acquisition, the WeightWorld brand expanded its European footprint by entering Poland, Finland and Portugal, and WeightWorld and Maxmedix were launched on Boots UK and established a presence on Amazon UAE. Internationally the Company continued to strengthen its footprint across the SAARC, Middle East & Africa, Southeast Asia and Indian Subcontinent Cluster regions through expansion into new geographies and region-specific innovation, and launched RiteBite Max Protein across nine international markets within the first year of that acquisition. Integration rather than construction drove domestic footprint work: the Company implemented rapid integration through the voluntary liquidation of Naturell (India) Private Limited, aligning operations with Zydus Wellness' enterprise-wide systems, distribution network and operating processes to unlock synergies across manufacturing, supply chain and go-to-market infrastructure. Capability build-out continued through the state-of-the-art R&D facility at Ahmedabad, which underpins a strong new product pipeline that could be launched at an appropriate time based on market requirements, and through a channel restructuring in which the Company transitioned from a distribution-led model to direct relationships with all modern trade and e-commerce partners, improving supply chain efficiency, product availability and lead times. Historical facility milestones referenced in the Corporate Overview are the new production facility in Sikkim - Unit-I and, later, the set-up of a new production facility in Sikkim - Unit-II alongside the launch of Sugar Free Green with Stevia; the physical distribution backbone comprises 25 integrated warehouses supporting both ambient and cold-chain categories.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on long-term structural growth drivers and portfolio diversification benefits; Pragmatic about short-term weather-related misses; Emphasizing data-driven decision making and AI-led marketing efficiency; Committed to profitable growth over blunt volume expansion.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Portfolio of trusted, category-leading brands built over 36+ years of operational excellence - Sugar Free, I'm lite, Glucon-D, Nutralite, Everyuth, Nycil, Complan, Cuticolor, RiteBite Max Protein, WeightWorld, Maxmedix and Animigo
- Retained leadership positions across most categories it operates in, including leadership in sugar substitutes
- Deep physical distribution: 25 integrated warehouses supporting ambient and cold-chain categories, 1,950+ distributors and 2,700+ feet-on-street representatives reaching approximately 2.8 million retail outlets
- Dedicated R&D centre at Ahmedabad supporting a broad spectrum of new product introductions and portfolio enhancements
- Diversified portfolio spanning nutrition, personal care and wellness that has progressively reduced dependence on season-specific demand cycles
- International presence across over 44 countries, broadened by the Comfort Click acquisition into the UK, EU and USA
- Overseas digital business platform and Direct-to-Consumer capability strengthened by Comfort Click's digital-first operating model
- Manufacturing plants accredited with FSSC 22000, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018 and GMP, validating process, quality consistency and food safety

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Weather dependency for ~30% of portfolio (Glucon-D/Nycil) causing quarterly volatility; Integration risks with international D2C operations; Currency fluctuation (GBP/EUR vs INR) impacting translated earnings; Intense competition in protein snacking and skincare segments; Regulatory changes in labor codes affecting cost structure.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 'seasonal' drag is masking a fundamentally stronger underlying business where normalized PAT grew 17% in Q4. The Comfort Click acquisition is already EPS accretive within 7 months, faster than typical integration timelines. Quick commerce is not just a channel but a strategic moat, contributing nearly half of all e-commerce sales and favoring Zydus's premium, small-pack, and impulse-buy SKUs over traditional general trade competitors.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [M&A-led growth] The milestone slide shows growth has been substantially acquisition-driven: Heinz India Private Limited, Carnation Nutra ("CNAFL"), Naturell (India) Private Limited, and Comfort Click Limited, UK and its 3 subsidiaries.
- [Reported vs adjusted] The deck leads with the adjusted measure: reported PAT of 1,189 INR mn was -7.0% YoY with PAT margin down to 8.3% from 14.9%, while Adjusted Net Profit of 1,679 INR mn was +26.5% and Adjusted EPS 5.28 vs 4.17 — two different readings of the same quarter, both as printed.
- [Weather-linked seasonality] A structurally weather-dependent portion of the portfolio: performance was "significantly impacted due to unseasonal rainfall in the North and East, key saliency markets", offsetting double-digit growth in West and South, compounded by cautious channel stocking and higher retailer inventory; the specific brand name for this slide is not recoverable from the extract.
- [Group linkage] Board ties to the parent group are explicit: Non-Executive Chairman Dr. Sharvil P. Patel is Managing Director of Zydus Lifesciences Limited, and Mr. Ganesh Nayak, Mr. Akhil Monappa and Mr. Kulin S. Lalbhai are also directors of Zydus Lifesciences Limited.
- [Market-share caveat] The deck itself warns that "High saliency and exceptional growth of online platforms is not reflected in market share", and several ranks in the table are "Mkt. Rank as per Company Estimates" rather than Nielsen/IQVIA.
